paper: Zang, Street & Koseff (1994), J. Comput. Phys. 114:18-33

questions.q: Does the collocated momentum-interpolation projection retain machine-precision face-flux divergence-freeness under extreme curvilinear grid distortion (high aspect ratio, high skewness, near-singular Jacobian), or does the Rhie-Chow-style face-flux recovery break down and re-admit odd-even pressure modes when the metric tensor becomes ill-conditioned?
questions.basis: This replication is Cartesian only (§5.3 caveat 3; C3 not tested). ZSK-1994's principal engineering-relevance claim is curvilinear correctness, but their published curvilinear cases use smooth, moderately-distorted meshes. The behaviour under industrial-grade skew (bent duct, wing-with-trailing-edge, sharp geometric transitions) is not established by either the paper or this replication.
next_steps: Implement the full contravariant-flux Jacobian metric bookkeeping and the metric-tensor Poisson operator described in ZSK §§2-3.
Run on a parametric mesh distortion sweep (aspect ratio 1..1000, max cell skew 0..85°) with a manufactured solution.
Track ||div U||_∞ vs distortion parameter; report the threshold at which the collocated projection loses machine precision or admits chequer-board modes.

questions.q: For time-dependent problems with moving/deforming boundaries, does the ZSK non-staggered fractional step outperform (in cost, in geometric-conservation-law compliance, in divergence quality) a modern staggered ALE (Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian) scheme, or does the ALE mesh-motion machinery negate the collocated-grid book-keeping advantage?
questions.basis: ZSK-1994 is a fixed-grid method. The engineering appeal of collocated grids is unstructured/moving-mesh generality, but the paper does not compare against staggered ALE, which is the modern standard for moving-boundary incompressible flow (biological pumping, FSI, free surface). Head-to-head evidence on the collocated-vs-staggered trade-off in the moving-mesh regime is missing.
next_steps: Set up a canonical FSI benchmark (oscillating cylinder at Re=100, Turek-Hron FSI2, or a piston-in-cavity) in both a ZSK-style collocated ALE and a staggered ALE.
Measure the geometric conservation law residual and the discrete divergence norm through the transient.
Compare wall-clock and per-timestep pressure-Poisson iteration counts.

questions.q: Can the ZSK fractional-step template be upgraded from its nominal first/second-order accuracy in time to a higher-order (BDF3, IMEX-RK3, pressure-correction of Timmermans-Van Kan type) projection while preserving the collocated momentum-interpolation face-flux divergence-freeness, or does the higher-order splitting error re-introduce pressure decoupling?
questions.basis: C4 (formal second-order accuracy) is not measured in this replication (§5.3 caveat 3; only one mesh N=128). Modern incompressible-flow practice increasingly demands 3rd-order-plus time integration for LES/DNS; whether the ZSK momentum-interpolation face-flux correction commutes with higher-order pressure-correction splitting is not answered by the 1994 paper.
next_steps: Derive the pressure-correction consistency condition for BDF3 combined with Rhie-Chow face-flux recovery.
Implement a manufactured-solution convergence study in Δt with fixed h and vice versa.
Verify that ||div U||_∞ remains at solver tolerance for each candidate splitting; discard any that leaks pressure modes.

questions.q: Does the non-staggered fractional-step scheme, when scaled to LES/DNS resolution on turbulent flow over topography (e.g. turbulent channel with wavy or rough lower wall), preserve enough kinetic-energy conservation to avoid spurious dissipation from the momentum-interpolation smoothing, or does the Rhie-Chow term act as an implicit numerical dissipation of the same character as an upwind bias?
questions.basis: The paper demonstrates the scheme on steady/low-Re cavity cases; this replication reaches only Re=1000, laminar, Cartesian. Rhie-Chow interpolation is known in the compressible-CFD literature to introduce an implicit fourth-derivative dissipation. Whether that dissipation is benign, tolerable, or fatal for a turbulence-resolving simulation on a curvilinear body-fitted mesh is not established.
next_steps: Set up a wall-resolved LES of turbulent channel flow (Re_τ ≈ 180 or 395) over a sinusoidal lower wall (established benchmark data from Cherukat et al. 1998, De Angelis et al. 1997).
Compare mean profiles, Reynolds stresses, and kinetic-energy spectra against a staggered reference DNS.
Quantify the effective Rhie-Chow dissipation by evaluating the energy budget term-by-term and reporting the spurious drain relative to the physical viscous dissipation.

questions.q: How does the ZSK non-staggered fractional step map onto modern multi-block, GPU-accelerated, unstructured-mesh production CFD codes — does the momentum-interpolation face-flux step admit an efficient block-parallel implementation, or does the implicit coupling between cell-centred velocity, face flux, and cell-centred pressure force serialised inter-block communication that erodes strong-scaling on GPU clusters?
questions.basis: This replication uses a direct sparse LU on the pressure Poisson equation on a single 128×128 mesh (§5.3 caveat 3), not the multigrid the paper mentions and not any parallel strategy. Modern production incompressible-CFD codes (OpenFOAM, Nek5000, PyFR) target multi-GPU multi-block; parallelisation of the collocated projection is an open engineering question with performance-critical answers.
next_steps: Port the momentum-interpolation face-flux and Poisson-projection kernels to CUDA/HIP or a portable framework (Kokkos, SYCL) on the uicgpu 8×A100 host.
Measure strong- and weak-scaling on a canonical multi-block curvilinear cavity or channel through 1..8 GPUs.
Compare against a staggered projection baseline of matched grid resolution; report per-DoF cost, communication volume, and any pressure-mode contamination from block-boundary interpolation.
